statement: In triangle $ABC$, angle $B$ measures $45^\circ$, angle $C$ measures $30^\circ$ and $AB = 6\sqrt{2}$. What is the length of $\overline{BC}$?

choices.misconception: I found the altitude $AD = 6$ correctly but treated it as the longer leg of the $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle, so I got $DC = \frac{6}{\sqrt{3}} = 2\sqrt{3}$ and $BC = 6 + 2\sqrt{3}$.

I used the $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ rule in the $45^\circ$ triangle and took $AD = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 6\sqrt{2} = 3\sqrt{2}$, so $BD = 3\sqrt{2}$, $DC = 3\sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{3} = 3\sqrt{6}$ and $BC = 3\sqrt{2} + 3\sqrt{6}$.
I found $AD = 6$ but then used the hypotenuse $AC = 2 \cdot 6 = 12$ as if it lay along $\overline{BC}$, so I got $BC = 6 + 12 = 18$.

hints: Triangle $ABC$ has no right angle, so make one. Drop a perpendicular from $A$ to $\overline{BC}$ and call its foot $D$.
The altitude splits $ABC$ into a $45^\circ$-$45^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle $ABD$ with hypotenuse $AB$ and a $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle $ADC$. Then $BC = BD + DC$.
In triangle $ABD$, $AD = BD = \frac{6\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 6$. In triangle $ADC$, $AD$ is opposite the $30^\circ$ angle, so it is the shorter leg and $DC = AD\sqrt{3}$.

solutions.reliable: Angle $A$ measures $180^\circ - 45^\circ - 30^\circ = 105^\circ$, so both angles at $B$ and $C$ are acute and the foot $D$ of the perpendicular from $A$ lies between $B$ and $C$. Triangle $ABD$ is a $45^\circ$-$45^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle with hypotenuse $AB = 6\sqrt{2}$, so $AD = BD = 6$. Triangle $ADC$ is a $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle with the $30^\circ$ angle at $C$, so $AD = 6$ is the shorter leg, $DC = 6\sqrt{3}$ and $AC = 12$. Therefore $BC = BD + DC = 6 + 6\sqrt{3} \approx 16.4$. Check with the law of sines: $\frac{AB}{\sin 30^\circ} = 12\sqrt{2}$ and $\frac{AC}{\sin 45^\circ} = \frac{12}{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}} = 12\sqrt{2}$, which agree.
